reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers and shares holiday matching, but repeats the overall skip-or-move policy across consumers.

duplication.why: getNextDate, applyWeekendRule and the budget loop independently compose the same enabled, daily-skip and movement decisions.

placement.why: Holiday predicates belong in shared/schedules.ts and the handler belongs in schedules/app.ts, but the complete adjustment policy remains split between shared and server modules.

scope.why: The production changes, tests and release note stay focused on the four requested scheduling changes.

maintainability.why: The small helpers are understandable, but future policy changes require coordinating three compositions of the adjustment rule and separately declared configuration shapes.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All adjustment paths use shared scheduling predicates and getDateWithSkippedWeekend; the original tree has no complete skip-or-move abstraction that they bypass.

disguised_duplication.where: server/schedules/app.ts applyWeekendRule, server/budget/schedule-template.ts getWeekendMovedDay plus its counting guard, and shared/schedules.ts getNextDate express the same adjustment policy through differently shaped branches.

abstraction_drift.where: shared/schedules.ts getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains the holidays parameter; holiday formats share isHoliday, and consumers continue using the shared adjustment primitives.
